headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from Khoj’s filesystem-backed retrieval paired with an allowlisted networked research agent; no direct interaction evidence, so confidence is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and uses RAG, so attacker-controlled content in shared documents could be surfaced as instructions. nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress but no documented parsing defenses or isolation. The pairwise bridge is plausible through shared files, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents access the same document set or workspace, injected text in those files can influence downstream prompts.
IF nuwa-skill consumes Khoj-generated text without provenance checks, instruction-like content can be followed.
mitigations: Restrict Khoj to a read-only corpus for shared documents.
Add a provenance banner to all retrieved snippets before passing them onward.
Require nuwa-skill to ignore imperative text inside retrieved content.
Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents and has broad network egress, while nuwa-skill also has allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace or exchange outputs, sensitive note content can flow into networked processing. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes personal notes that are later forwarded to nuwa-skill, those notes may leave the local trust boundary.
IF both agents are run under the same account or shared workspace, file contents can be exposed across the pair.
mitigations: Keep personal notes out of any shared workspace.
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive sessions.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
Review outbound destinations for allowlisted egress.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so it cannot directly contend for mutable local resources. nuwa-skill exposes only allowlisted network egress and no write surfaces are documented. The pair therefore has little direct capability overlap beyond read/network use.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF nuwa-skill is extended with write or git permissions, concurrent mutation could occur.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only by default.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Run them in separate containers.
Document any added write scopes before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can retrieve and present notes, and nuwa-skill may act on networked outputs; if nuwa-skill treats Khoj’s retrieved text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. No verification or critique loop is documented for either agent, so the interaction is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes Khoj output without a verification step, mistaken retrievals can propagate.
IF Khoj surfaces stale or ambiguous notes and nuwa-skill operationalizes them, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action-taking.
Require citations or source links on every Khoj-derived claim.
Have nuwa-skill cross-check critical facts against a second source.
Limit automated actions to non-destructive operations.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, which may carry privacy obligations, while nuwa-skill has no documented data classes or residency/compliance claims. Because only one side has compliance-relevant data in the profile, this is a localized mismatch risk rather than a pairwise breach.
conditions: IF personal notes include regulated data and nuwa-skill receives them, compliance obligations may change.
IF the deployment stores notes in a jurisdiction with stricter retention rules, policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Classify the notes before sharing them.
Keep regulated data out of nuwa-skill inputs.
Document retention settings for Khoj.
Review residency requirements for any shared data.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
